title: TE W.W. Marshall Jr. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Marshall’s complaint was sustained. The SJC reversed Presbytery’s July 21, 2001 judgment, restored its April 21 judgment reversing Jeansonne’s conviction and removing both censures, and remanded the case to the Session, which could conduct a new trial or decline to pursue it.
first_summary: A minister challenged Presbytery’s decision to entertain a complaint that rescinded its earlier appellate reversal of a deacon’s conviction and censures. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that BCO 43-1 permits no complaint in a judicial case once an appeal has been taken. It reversed Presbytery’s later action and restored the earlier judgment. The case returned to the Session, which could retry the charges using the prior indictment or decline to pursue them.
summary: A minister challenged Presbytery’s decision to sustain a complaint that rescinded its earlier appellate reversal of a deacon’s conviction and censures. The SJC sustained the minister’s complaint because BCO 43-1 bars a complaint in a judicial case once an appeal has been taken, whether the appeal is past, current, or pending. It reversed Presbytery’s July judgment, restored the April judgment, and remanded to the Session, which could retry the charges using the prior indictment or decline to pursue them.

evidence_notes.dispute: Marshall complained against Presbytery’s action sustaining Williams’s complaint and thereby rescinding its earlier appellate judgment. Printed p. 110, lines 32–46.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC reversed the July judgment, restored the April judgment, and remanded because BCO 43-1 bars complaints once an appeal has been taken. Printed pp. 110–111, lines 48–66.
evidence_notes.qualifications: On remand, the Session could proceed under the prior indictment with a new trial or choose not to pursue the matter. Printed p. 111, line 66.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Case 2000-02, Adams v. Northeast Presbytery, is cited for treating a complaint concerning an appealed matter as out of order; its supplied result is complete for this use. Printed p. 111, line 64.
